Q: Why does getting element contents via jQuery require a .remove() statement? A:

In order, it does this:

  1. Create a new empty DIV object (not in the DOM yet)
  2. Find the "#top" object in your page
  3. Clone that "#top" object.
  4. Append this clone to the previously created DIV object
  5. Remove the whole DIV object from the DOM and clean up any jQuery related data to any of the objects
  6. Get the innerHTML of the DIV object

The one thing that the .remove() does here is clean up any jQuery data associated with any objects in the tree that wouldn't otherwise happen at this point.

In your examples A and B, there is technically not supposed to be a difference between the two. In practice, I've found a few bugs in older versions of IE with option B. jQuery seems to follow a code path involving document fragments and I've seen some problems with that.

Q: Python treemap with first level as color and legend rather than labels A:

If you are just wanting to remove the spacing between squares completely, setting the parameter of squarify.plot(... pad=False) will suffice. But I noticed your examples still had spacing even though you said what you had 'are not grouped together', so you don't want it completely removed?

I am also noticing that your examples put everything into column groups. Do you not want overlapping columns like this?:

If you want really narrow 'borders', then add a line border and make the line border match the background color:

pad=False,
linewidth=1,
edgecolor="white",

You can use this for the legend:

import matplotlib.patches as mpatches

legend_patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=colors[i], label=city[i]) for i in range(len(city))]

plt.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.10, 1))

Adjust parameters of bbox_to_anchor if you want to shift the legend outside the boundaries of the squarify display. The legend might get clipped depending on where you put it, so add plt.tight_layout() before plt.show() if you want to auto adjust the view window to not cut off the legend.
